summary: Retested FIX#4 visfAtlas after inlining VISFATLAS_COLORMAP and registering it synchronously at niivue init. The async race is fixed (colormap IS registered before user toggle, state correctly stores 'visfAtlas'), BUT the categorical multi-hue rendering still FAILS. All 33 ROIs render as one blue gradient — no red faces, no yellow hMT, no green bodies — indicating niivue is interpolating the 34-entry LUT as a continuous colormap instead of treating it as 34 discrete labels. Two additional regressions surfaced: (a) the COLORMAPS select dropdown in LayerControl has a hardcoded options array that does not include 'visfAtlas' or 'polar_angle', so [data-testid=colormap-visfAtlas].value falls back to 'gray' (display bug, state is correct); (b) [data-testid=crosshair-labels] does not exist anywhere in the DOM; only crosshair-toggle / crosshair-info / crosshair-mm are present. Crosshair VISFATLAS column also reads 0 at every clicked location, even on visibly colored occipital voxels.

ui_bugs.issue: Hardcoded COLORMAPS list (lines 5-22) is missing 'visfAtlas' and 'polar_angle'. The <select value={colormap}> therefore has no matching <option>, so its .value silently falls back to the first option ('gray'). The right-aligned text label shows the correct value ('visfAtlas'), but the dropdown is misleading and breaks any test reading select.value. Verified: select.options has 16 entries, none are 'visfAtlas'.

Even though nv.addColormap('visfAtlas', VISFATLAS_COLORMAP) is now called synchronously at init (verified — race condition fixed, state.colormap === 'visfAtlas'), the rendered overlay is still a near-monochromatic blue gradient across all 33 ROIs. The colormap inlined has I=[0..34] with hues spanning red (faces, entry 1: R=255,G=0,B=0), yellow (hMT, entry 11: R=254,G=217,B=118), and various greens — none of these appear in the brain overlay. Likely cause: niivue treats arbitrary R/G/B/A/I/labels colormaps as continuous LUTs (interpolated to 256 entries across cal_min..cal_max). For a 34-label discrete atlas you need either (a) vol.colormapLabel = {...} with the labels payload, (b) per-label setting of vol.cmap via nv.setCustomColormap with isLabel:true, or (c) build a 256-entry cmap with step-function R/G/B so each integer index maps to its categorical hue exactly.

Spec requires [data-testid=crosshair-labels] to show region name (e.g. 'lh_v1v_retinotopic') when crosshair sits on a labeled voxel. This element does not exist anywhere in the DOM after toggling visfAtlas. Only crosshair-toggle, crosshair-info, crosshair-mm are present. Either the component was never added or it is gated on a condition that is not being met.

[data-testid=crosshair-values] VISFATLAS column reads 0 at every tested click location (4 occipital + temporal points). MNI152 base values change correctly (63→74→70), confirming clicks land on different voxels, but the visfAtlas overlay returns 0 each time. Suggests either (a) the overlay volume is loaded with wrong voxel-grid alignment and clicks land on zero voxels, or (b) the readout code reads from the wrong NVImage instance.

integration_issues.issue: The race condition fix is verified working (cmap registered synchronously, no async fetch involved), but discrete-label semantics are missing. Niivue's nv.addColormap(name, {R,G,B,A,I,labels}) registers a continuous LUT — the labels array does not by itself produce stepwise categorical rendering. Recommended fix: either (1) expand the inlined cmap to a 256-entry step-function where indices 0-7 = entry 0 color, 8-15 = entry 1 color, … (255 entries / 34 labels ≈ 7 per label), and set vol.cal_min=0, vol.cal_max=34; or (2) use niivue's label-volume API by setting vol.colormapLabel = {R,G,B,A,labels} directly on the volume after add and calling nv.setColormapLabel(id, payload).

action_items: Fix categorical rendering — niivue's plain addColormap does not produce stepwise label rendering. Use one of: (a) inflate VISFATLAS_COLORMAP to a 256-entry step LUT keyed on integer label index (each of the 34 entries repeated ~7 times in I/R/G/B), set vol.cal_min=0, vol.cal_max=34 on add; (b) on overlay add, set vol.colormapLabel = { R,G,B,A,labels } from the imported VISFATLAS_COLORMAP and re-call nv.updateGLVolume(); or (c) use nv.setColormapLabel(volId, labels) once the overlay is attached. Option (b) most faithfully matches niivue's documented label-volume API.

Add 'visfAtlas' (and 'polar_angle') to the COLORMAPS array in /app/frontend/src/components/LayerControl.jsx so the <select> can actually display the active value and round-trip it on user change. Currently the right-hand text label is decorative only.

Implement [data-testid=crosshair-labels] block: when the visfAtlas overlay is loaded and the crosshair sits over a labeled voxel, read the integer value, look up the matching string in VISFATLAS_COLORMAP.labels, and render it in a new <div data-testid='crosshair-labels'>. Conditional gating on the layer being visible is fine, but it must appear when a labeled overlay is on.

Debug why crosshair VISFATLAS value reads 0 at clicked occipital voxels — verify the overlay NVImage's voxel grid alignment with MNI152 and that the readout code is targeting vol.volume[idx] of the visfAtlas volume, not a stale reference.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE OF REMAINING FAILURE: VISFATLAS_COLORMAP is registered via nv.addColormap('visfAtlas', {R,G,B,A,I,labels}). Niivue's addColormap interprets this as a continuous LUT (interpolated to 256 entries across vol.cal_min..vol.cal_max). The integer label volume (values 0..33) is then mapped through this LUT, but because the LUT only has 35 control points spanning the full cal range, niivue interpolates between control points — so adjacent label values blend rather than picking the exact hue. With cal_min=0 cal_max=33 the integer values 0,1,2,…,33 would land near control points i=0..33 in the I array, so it should in theory work — BUT niivue normalises I (control-point indices) onto 0..255, not onto cal range, when a 'labels' array is supplied without setting colormapLabel separately. The visible behavior (mostly blue with subtle gradient) matches what happens when a 34-entry LUT is interpolated/oversampled and the dark-blue retinotopic family (entries 12-17) happens to dominate the visible cortex. PROPER FIX: set vol.colormapLabel = VISFATLAS_COLORMAP on the volume after addOverlayFromUrl, then nv.updateGLVolume() and drawScene(). This is the documented niivue API for discrete label volumes.
